Autism

One mouse study was identified. It provides preclinical evidence only and does not establish a treatment effect in autistic people.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

One mouse study was identified. It provides preclinical evidence only and does not establish a treatment effect in autistic people.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact Brain > Autism category contains ten titles: six human primary reports, one mouse study, two reviews, and one editorial. The human records include three randomized reports and three nonrandomized reports. Protocols include transcranial PBM and laser acupuncture, which should not be treated as equivalent. The category also includes publications linked to the same trial registry.

Human and clinical evidence

Fradkin et al. randomized 30 children aged two to six years in a sham-controlled transcranial PBM trial using 850-nm light at 40 Hz for eight weeks. The reported between-group CARS change was 7.23 points (2024). A 2025 open-label report included 23 participants, 22 of whom completed treatment, and reported a similar CARS reduction; it is linked to the same NCT04660552 registry, so participant overlap or a related cohort cannot be ruled out (Fradkin et al. 2025). A 2023 randomized laser-acupuncture report and a 2018 low-level laser report add human publications but use different protocols and do not independently replicate the transcranial study (Elsheikh et al. 2023 Leisman et al. 2018). The small sample sizes and short-term symptom scales do not establish durable changes in communication, daily function, or quality of life.

Animal evidence

One mouse publication was identified in the category. It is an experimental model and does not establish clinical efficacy or dosing in children.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No standalone in-vitro or ex-vivo publication was identified.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

Human studies use different transcranial or acupuncture-point approaches, wavelengths, schedules, and comparators. The 850-nm sham-controlled protocol is not interchangeable with laser acupuncture or open-label treatment. CARS changes should be interpreted alongside blinded functional measures and longer follow-up; registry linkage alone does not prove that two reports contain the same participants.

Interpretation

A small sham-controlled study provides a preliminary signal, but the evidence base is heterogeneous and replication is limited. The open-label report is linked to the same registry and cannot by itself establish independent confirmation or durable functional benefit.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow for short-term changes in selected autism symptom scores with transcranial PBM Very low for durable functional benefit or replicated efficacy
Publications and records10 exact-category titles.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

A small sham-controlled trial reported a short-term symptom-score difference, but the broader category includes small acupuncture and open-label studies with varied methods. A later open-label report is linked to the same trial registry as the sham study, so independence is uncertain. Larger preregistered trials with longer follow-up and functional outcomes are needed.
